title: The moon trees of Mississippi
body: Many of my online acquaintances know that I live in Chicago, but I suspect they might not know that I’m from a small university town in Mississippi called Starkville.

title: The Cascade
body: Hearty congrats to Robin Rendle who has turned his wonderful CSS-focused newsletter into a good, old fashioned blog. The Cascade is beautiful, and is already full of great content for CSS nerds like me.

title: Boku no Natsuyasumi
body: Several months ago, in an issue of Spencer Chang’s newsletter, I discovered the 6 hour video review of a game called Boku no Natsuyasumi by Tim Rogers (known as Action Button).

title: Poets of the mundane
body: Paul has always been my favorite Beatle.

title: Apps and the Age of AI
body: For how much software has evolved and matured I find it strange how many tasks remain unaddressed by niche, purpose-built software. I’m always excited to see how novel ideas can come about from focusing in on a narrow domain.

title: Conjurings of the harvest moon
body: Autumn is my favorite time of the year. The trees outside my apartment here in Oak Park are shining gold, and the air is starting to feel crisp and cold. Sweater weather, if you will.

title: The eyes and ears of AI
body: It’s hard to keep up with the progress of AI. It seems as though every week there’s a new breakthrough or advancement that seemingly changes the game. Each step forward brings both a sense of wonder and a feeling of dread.

title: Every day is science fiction
body: Science fiction is one of my favorite genres because of its power to make the strange familiar and the familiar strange.

title: How blogs shaped the web
body: I have a lot of nostalgia for the era of blogging that I grew up with during the first decade or so of the 2000s.

title: Ambient internet
body: The recent fad of the metaverse is all about digitizing the physical world and moving our shared experiences (even more so) onto the internet.

title: Where it all began
body: I remember the first time I saw a Mac in person. I was in middle school, but on the campus of the nearby college because my dad had a gig as a stand-in drummer for a local band.

title: Footprints in the Martian sand
body: Since I was a kid the space program has been an object of my fascination, and even as an adult I’ve been captured by the heroics of NASA and other organizations launching probes and telescopes into the far reaches of space.
